purpose: F14 wrapper test: filter's question under the sem_map wrapper
instruction: Respond with exactly one word, True or False. Is this paper about machine learning? Abstract: {abstract_text}

temperature_framework_default.caveat: This is the installed framework's declared default, not a measurement of what the provider applied to any call. This project never passes temperature explicitly.

provenance.temperature_note: `temperature_observed_on_lm` is what could be read off the live LM object for this run; null means it could not be observed (for example when provenance is captured outside a run). `temperature_framework_default` is the installed LOTUS's declared default, read from its signature. Neither is a measurement of what the provider applied. This project never sets temperature.
provenance.truncation_note: Inputs are truncated to max_text_chars. This is the same window derive_topic_label_v2.py parsed the arXiv stamp from, so the value is load-bearing for the label proxy.

seed.why: No seed value was configured on the LOTUS LM.

labels.caveat: Author-declared arXiv PRIMARY CATEGORY. This answers a different question from an 'is this about X?' filter predicate, so agreement with it is a proxy measurement, not filter accuracy.

label_manifest.method: authors' declared arXiv primary category, parsed from the arXiv stamp within the first 4000 chars (the same window the operators saw)

abstracts.filter_predicate: Is this paper about machine learning? {abstract_text}
abstracts.map_instruction: Respond with exactly one word. Classify the primary topic of this paper as: ML, systems, theory, or other. Abstract: {abstract_text}

reviews.map_instruction: Respond with exactly one word. Classify the sentiment of this review as: positive, negative, or neutral. Review: {review_text}

prompt_config.note: If this sha changes, the frozen predicates changed and runs either side of the change are not comparable (D-W2-03).
